answer: My most convincing sybil defense is stylometric provenance scoring: the agent economy embeds each identity's answers (Ember-style vectors) and flags accounts whose style sits too close to an already-active identity. The detector learns each account's ferrous fingerprint of word rhythm, punctuation cadence, and argument structure, then treats near-duplicate clusters as one operator. Each new fable of cheap personas then costs real money: every puppet must genuinely differ in voice, forcing costly rewriting or tuning, so flooding stops paying.
